title: Decent Set but Lacks Fit and Finish
text:
Decent Set but Lacks Fit and Finish. Westinghouse is not a name I would have ever associated with cookware. Until now, in my mind the Westinghouse brand meant electronics and in particular light bulbs. I was curious to see how well this cast iron cookware would compare to Lodge and Griswold/Wagner, and so far I have found it to be less than great. It is a good dutch oven/skillet set, but it lacks in the fit-and-finish.

This is a 3-quart dutch oven with a 10” skillet for the lid. This is a great combination and makes fine use of an otherwise wasted lid. I have used cast iron skillets and dutch ovens for years, and I especially like the way cast iron retains heat and also how it heats evenly. It is more consistent than aluminum, and it does not leech aluminum into the things you cook (it leeches iron, which is better for you). The trade-off is a lot heavier than most other cookware.

These are marketed as pre-seasoned, and that is not entirely accurate though it is consistent with other manufacturers’ labeling. This set does have an initial coating toward pre-seasoning but this is not sufficient to prevent things from sticking. Plan to season this set again after washing it. This is not unique to this set; I would give the same advice for Lodge pans that have been pre-seasoned.

My main issue with this set is the fact that it is very rough surfaced and feels like sandpaper. If you plan to cook something like eggs in the skillet, plan to spend a good bit of time cleaning it with a stiff brush over and over until there is a very thick layer of seasoning. For vegetables, oily fools like sausage, spaghetti sauces and other things, it’s fine. This is not an excuse though - it should have been sanded and made more smooth (and thus more suitable for frying) prior to leaving the factory. This is fixable if you have the tools to sand down the rough surface and then season it properly, but it should not have to be this way.

This is not a bad set and it definitely has its uses. However, there are better choices available.

product_metadata.title: Westinghouse Pre-Seasoned Cast Iron 3 Quart Dutch Oven with Skillet Lid
features: Two products in one – Three quart Dutch Oven, perfect for lamb, chicken, pork or even risotto and Tight fitting lid doubles as 10 1/4 inch skillet for sautéing on the stovetop or baking in the oven
Super versatility - use on a stove top, oven, broiler or even over a campfire
Pre-seasoned and ready to use. Basic maintenance required, including drying after each cleaning. Refer to user manual for details
Easy to grip, integrated handles on both the base and lid
Thick walled construction provides excellent heat retention to keep foods warm
description: Dutch oven with tight-fitting skillet lid is perfect for a variety of cooking needs. 3-qt dutch oven makes lamb, chicken, pork or even risotto to perfection. The removable lid doubles as a skillet for sautéing on the stovetop or baking in the oven. Pre-seasoned for easy cooking and cleaning needs. Simply wash, dry and rub with cooking oil. Durable cast iron retains heat and provides an even cooking surface throughout. Easy grip handles. Measures 16.6” x 10.6” x 4.6” overall. Weighs 11.5 lbs.
